title: Preserve Skill policy denial when approval is also required
goal: Ensure SkillRuntime reports an explicit policy denial before considering the separate approval requirement.
context: SkillRuntime currently checks requiresApproval before allowed. If a policy returns allowed=false and requiresApproval=true, the runtime reports policyRequiresApproval rather than policyDenied; callers could mistake an explicit denial for a request that user approval can satisfy.
forbidden_changes: Do not let approval satisfy an explicit policy denial.
Do not weaken the separate approval requirement when policy allows an action.
Do not invoke the executor when policy denies.
acceptance_criteria: A decision with allowed=false and requiresApproval=true throws policyDenied with the policy reason.
A decision with allowed=true and requiresApproval=true still throws policyRequiresApproval.
Regression uses executeVerified and proves denied Skill execution does not return output.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: Check decision.allowed first, then handle requiresApproval only for policy-approved actions; assert the precise policyDenied error.
